question: What is the primary goal of occupational health and safety in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Reducing financial costs of medical supplies
options.B: Enforcing strict disciplinary rules for staff
options.C: Protecting the well-being of all workers
options.D: Increasing daily hospital patient admission rates

explanation: Occupational health prioritizes safeguarding the physical, mental, and social welfare of employees while they perform their duties. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h1)

question: Who shares the responsibility for maintaining a safe working environment?

options.A: Patients receiving care in the facility

explanation: Both management and staff must actively collaborate to identify hazards and adhere to established safety protocols. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h1)

question: What is the most effective intervention level in the hierarchy of controls?
explanation: Physically removing a hazard provides the highest level of protection because it completely removes the risk of exposure. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h2)

question: Why is personal protective equipment considered the last line of defense?

options.A: It is the most expensive method for hospital management
options.B: It relies heavily on human behavior and correct usage
options.C: It completely removes the hazard from the environment
options.D: It eliminates the need for any administrative policies

explanation: PPE does not alter the actual hazard in the environment; if worn incorrectly or damaged, the worker remains fully exposed. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h2)

question: Installing a biological safety cabinet in a hospital laboratory is an example of which control?
explanation: Physical equipment modifications that isolate the worker from hazards fall directly under engineering controls. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h3)

question: Rotating nurses out of high-risk infectious units is designed to achieve what outcome?

options.A: Providing a physical barrier against sharp injuries
options.B: Eliminating the biological agent from the hospital
options.C: Replacing a dangerous procedure with a safer task
options.D: Reducing the duration of exposure to pathogens

explanation: Limiting the time an individual spends in a hazardous zone minimizes their cumulative risk of contracting an infection. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h3)

question: What action must a nurse take immediately after removing a pair of examination gloves?

options.C: Put on a clean lab coat

explanation: Microscopic pores or accidental contamination during removal mean hands must always be cleaned immediately after taking off gloves. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h4)

question: Why is the correct sequence for removing personal protective equipment strictly enforced?

options.A: To speed up the process of leaving an isolation room
options.B: To prevent self-contamination during the undressing process
options.C: To ensure the items can be washed and reused safely
options.D: To comply with uniform color codes in the ward

explanation: Following a standardized doffing order stops infectious agents on the outside of the gear from touching skin or scrubs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a pre-employment medical examination in occupational health?

options.A: Ensuring the worker never falls ill on duty
options.B: Establishing a baseline health status for the worker
options.C: Determining the exact monthly salary of the staff
options.D: Fulfilling insurance requirements for hospital management

explanation: Initial health checks provide a reference point to compare against if future health issues arise from workplace exposures. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h5)

question: Why are routine immunizations tracked for healthcare workers in clinical facilities?

options.A: To comply with international travel visa guidelines
options.B: To protect staff from preventable infectious agents on duty
options.C: To replace the need for engineering and administrative controls
options.D: To prevent patients from bringing new diseases into the ward

explanation: Vaccines build active immunity against biological hazards like hepatitis B that workers frequently encounter in practice. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h5)

question: What body mechanics principle should a nurse apply when lifting a heavy object?

options.A: Hold the heavy load far away from the body center
options.B: Twist the spine quickly to gain sudden momentum
options.C: Bend at the knees and keep the back straight
options.D: Keep legs straight and bend forward at the waist

explanation: Using leg muscles instead of lower back muscles prevents undue strain on the spinal column during lifting tasks. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h6)

question: Musculoskeletal disorders among nurses are most commonly linked to which workplace activity?

options.A: Administering oral medications to stable clients
options.B: Writing patient notes in the medical records
options.C: Participating in routine ward handover meetings

explanation: Frequent manual handling of patients places heavy physical stress on the back and joints of healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h6)

question: Which practice is strictly prohibited when handling used injection needles to prevent injuries?
explanation: Hand recapping is a leading cause of accidental needle-stick punctures and is strictly prohibited in safety guidelines. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h7)

question: Standard precautions in a healthcare setting must be applied to which group of individuals?

options.A: Only patients diagnosed with known blood-borne viruses
options.B: Patients admitted exclusively to the intensive care unit
options.C: Individuals showing visible symptoms of respiratory illness
options.D: All patients regardless of their infection status

explanation: Standard precautions treat all body fluids as potentially infectious to protect staff from unrecognized pathogen carriers. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h7)

question: A community health nurse visiting a local factory is primarily responsible for doing what?

options.A: Taking over the management and financial ownership of the factory
options.B: Assessing environmental hazards and educating workers on safety
options.C: Replacing all factory machinery with modern digital computers
options.D: Manufacturing protective gear for sale to the industrial staff

explanation: Community health nurses inspect work environments to spot risks and teach workers how to protect themselves from injury. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h8)

question: Which activity is a key part of occupational health nursing in non-hospital settings?

options.B: Providing first aid and health education
options.C: Filing tax returns for industrial businesses

explanation: Nurses in occupational roles respond to workplace injuries with first aid and conduct teaching sessions to prevent future incidents. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h8)
